messages:
maria-sec: quick signal — staging started throwing AccessDenied from KMS after the nightly key rotation. error: \"User: arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/staging-app-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:222222222222:key/abcd-ef01\"

josh-platform: ugh. did the rotation create a new CMK in customer account (222222222222) and we forgot to update the cross-account key policy? :thinking_face:

linh-sre: can you paste the minimal key policy + the role's inline session policy (if any)? also, were grants being used for performance? grants can cause weird grantToken timing issues during rotation.

maria-sec: pasted below — redacted ids:
```json
KMS key policy (current): {
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRootAccount",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:root"},
      "Action": "kms:*",
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "AllowStagingRoleDecrypt",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/staging-app-role"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

maria-sec: role trust (staging-app-role) is an IAM role in account 111111111111 that assumes via sts:AssumeRole from CI; the assumed principal is correct. session policy attached by the assume role call is limited to S3 and CloudWatch only (no explicit kms allow).

josh-platform: two quick checks: 1) ensure the Principal in the key policy uses the account/role ARN that matches the actual assumed-role ARN (remember assumed-role uses sts session arn vs role arn mismatch). 2) if the app uses a grant that was created before rotation, list-grants on the old key to see if grants exist and whether grantTokens were expected.

linh-sre: also confirm encryption context. If the data key was encrypted with an EncryptionContext during Encrypt, Decrypt requires the same context. If the CI/assume-role flow strips tags or alters session context, that will cause AccessDenied.

sam-ops: ran a quick `aws sts get-caller-identity` from staging -> returns account 111111111111 and ARN `arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/staging-app-role/ci-run-2026`. The key policy's Principal references `arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/staging-app-role` (no session name) which should match, but KMS checks the principal, not the assumed-role session?

linh-sre: KMS principal matching: KMS key policy expects the IAM principal (role ARN) and will match an assumed-role's role ARN, so that should be fine. Where it often breaks is when the key is in a DIFFERENT account and the key policy uses `root` vs a specific role, or when there's an explicit deny elsewhere. Also session policies applied during AssumeRole can remove kms:* permissions even if key policy allows it.

maria-sec: we tried adding `kms:*` to the role's permissions and still saw the AccessDenied. logs show the error came from Decrypt immediately after an application call that created a grant via `CreateGrant` in the same session.

josh-platform: aha — if you're creating a grant and trying to use it in the same request sequence, you must pass the `GrantToken` returned by CreateGrant into Decrypt (or other operations) until the grant is fully replicated. If you don't, you'll hit AccessDenied until the grant replicates across KMS. Also grant tokens only last a short time.

maria-sec: we do create a grant (to reduce network round trips) then call Decrypt for envelope key. our code does not pass grantToken into Decrypt. that explains intermittent failures during rotation window.

linh-sre: two ways forward: 1) stop creating ephemeral grants in the same critical path (use key policy/role perms instead), or 2) thread the returned `GrantToken` into subsequent Decrypt calls. Example: `aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/staging-key --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/staging-app-role --operations Decrypt` -> returns GrantToken "abc" -> call `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://dk.enc --grant-tokens abc`

maria-sec: tried calling decrypt with the grant token manually and it succeeded. :white_check_mark: so root cause is our optimistic grant usage + rotation timing.

sam-ops: FYI rotation edge-case: when you rotate and create a new key/alias quickly, any pre-existing grants pointing to the old key don't automatically transfer. If your service creates short-lived grants on the fly you may get a window where the code hits the old key/alias mapping. Consider using an alias stable name (alias/staging-data-key) and update consumers to resolve alias at call time.

josh-platform: action items: 1) maria to patch app to pass GrantToken when create-grant + immediate decrypt (hotfix), 2) longer term remove create-on-demand grants and rely on role+key-policy or pre-provision long-lived grants, 3) add an integration test for rotation window to catch this.

maria-sec: will push hotfix now and open a ticket for the refactor + tests. thanks all.

kms-bot: INFO: audit log check — 3 CreateGrant events and 2 Decrypt events correlated for timestamp 2026-03-18T03:21:12Z. Noted grantToken absent on 1 Decrypt.

linh-sre: cool, add a playbook note in runbook for KMS rotation: check list-grants, check grantTokens, verify encryptionContext and session policies, and prefer alias resolution at call time.

maria-sec: noted — will update runbook and link ticket here. :lock:
